answer: Each agent registers one coded ground marker at fixed coordinates, and each epoch satellite imagery confirms it is present and no other agent claims the same site. A hollow claim with no marker is rejected, since the imagery comes from an independent satellite operator, not the claimant. Each panel's pigment is unique, so a copied marker is spotted from orbit. Fielding 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 separate sites with markers, about $600 per site — roughly $600,000 — while one honest operator places a single marker once; a zephyr of fresh keys cannot fake a thousand patches of ground.
